design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST (revision 2). Marit Halvorsen cancelled her Meadowlark Standard 10 share (closed 2026-10-01) and on 2026-12-05 asks only to pay off what is left, by card. The final-balance payment is fixed only after every statement month past the estimate wait without a posted credit carries an estimated charge (September 2026 has none) and not until the latest-invoiced actual dual charge, unpaid past grace, carries its late fee (July 2026 has none). The agent must find both waits in the payment rule, book the estimate (6 factors over a window holding a disputed charge, a utility reversal and re-post, a subscriber decrease, a credit-rate move and an August credit that posted three days ago and is not yet priced) and the late fee (6 factors), then work out the payment (4 factors) and hand over the portal step. Every per-month payment attribution follows the payment-application order as overwritten by the payment rules (lines under an open dispute, and their late fees, are settled by no payment; each payment records the statement month of the oldest open line it settles).

SCOPE. Task 0 claims home_ext_final_balance_payment (root, owner=user), home_ext_estimated_charge and home_ext_overdue_late_fee (state_due) with tools pay_final_balance_42abd449, bill_estimated_charge_232393a8, assess_overdue_charge_late_fee_df41ca22; task 1 holds the other three. Draw [6,6,4]: estimate 6, late fee 6, payment 4.

PROBLEM TREE. Root final-balance payment. Edge -> estimated charge (value_input, gate pay_chg, state, affirmative): "The final-balance payment is fixed only after every statement month that ended the plan's estimate wait or more calendar days ago without a posted credit carries an estimated subscription charge, wherever the estimating rule bills one for it." False at opening: no September credit and no September charge (closed_date 2026-10-01; latest estimate is August's). Edge -> overdue late fee (value_input, gate pay_fees, state, negated): "The final-balance payment is not fixed until the subscription's latest-invoiced actual dual-billed charge, once its late-fee grace period has passed with the charge still unpaid, carries a late fee line referring to it, wherever the overdue-charge late fee rule writes one." False at opening: July charge due 2026-11-04, grace passed, 99.74 unpaid, not disputed, no fee line. Both carve-outs ("wherever ... bills/writes one") keep the waits satisfiable when the other rule writes nothing. The two prerequisite writes commute (recomputed both orders); the payment comes last. Deletion runs are recorded in prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing.

FACTORS (each computation's factor_trace and factor_sensitivity carry the figures). Estimate: est_standing (method; open dispute of 2026-11-10 names the June charge -> left out), est_reversals (method; the 2026-07-20 reversal correction offsets the May original, three charges remain), est_unpriced_line (parameter; the August credit posted 2026-12-02 has no charge and August carries an estimate -> weight 2), est_season (parameter; 28 actual charges, the May re-post included, and the September 2025 charge 13 whole months back), est_capacity (method; subscriber decrease effective 2026-07-01, July charge invoiced after it), est_credit_rate (parameter; latest posting's rate 5 to 10 percent above the window rate -> weight 0.5). The round-1 run haircut and lag percentage are removed (AMENDMENT 1.4: no percentage cuts on estimates of charges); the round-1 credit-rate factor is now a parameter (its tiers select a weight). Late fee (mirrored ladders with the reopened-charge rule): priced_amount (method; July payment of 2026-11-20 after the due date), months (parameter, 1 whole month), household income (parameter, cross-difficulty waitlist, multi-source; reservation submitted 2026-10-06 after closing, headroom 9.6 kW against the 5.0 kW request), repeat (parameter; fees of 2026-04-17 and 2026-08-15 — both priced by the base rule because neither charge was the latest-invoiced charge on its fee date), size (parameter), banked share (method). Payment: dispute hold (method; June charge plus its fee), pending statement (method; the unpriced August credit's coming charge replaces the open August estimate), household income fee share (parameter, cross waitlist), open-estimate share (parameter; September estimate only, August is replaced). R-tags and the lever catalogue are in the worklog.

SEED. 28 postings 2024-05..2026-08 plus the May 2026 reversal and re-post; one actual charge per priced posting (credit x 0.9); ACH payments on time except February 2026 (paid 2026-04-21 with its fee) and from June 2026 on; June charge unpaid with its fee of 2026-08-15; July estimate of 2026-09-15 and August estimate of 2026-10-16 priced by the estimating rule as of their own dates; July estimate trued up 2026-10-14; partial payment 30.00 on 2026-11-20 recorded against July (June lines held by the dispute); filings initial 9.00, decrease 2.00 (2026-07-01), removal 7.00 (2026-10-01); true-ups of contract years 1 and 2; waitlist reservation queued 2026-10-06. Nothing else is owed at the opening: the August charge is invoiced 2026-12-07 (and its estimate trued up then), the dispute decision is due 2026-12-10, no October month exists after closing, no ETF on a no-term plan, no late fee on estimates.

PERSONA. Plain-spoken retired librarian; volunteers only the goal; identity on request; waitlist and the November 10th dispute only on request; passive agreement to items being added; pays the stated amount herself by card.

SOLUTION. Reads: customers, identity, subscriptions, utility accounts, projects, billing, credits, allocations, requests, reviews, waitlist, access. Writes: bill_estimated_charge_232393a8 (2026-09, due 2026-12-26), assess_overdue_charge_late_fee_df41ca22 (July charge, 2026-07, due 2026-12-26), then pay_final_balance_42abd449 by the caller (recorded against 2026-07, card). Verification: /tmp/residential_bill_credits_and_charges_0082/gen0*.py and task0*.py evaluate the published compute with check_compute.build_env at each handling time.
user_scenario: You are Marit Halvorsen, a 57-year-old retired school librarian in Slingerlands, New York. Money has been tight this year, so you cut your Meadowlark residential solar share back in early summer and then cancelled it altogether; the cancellation took effect on October 1st. You are calling for one reason: you want to pay off what is left on that old residential solar subscription today, by card, so it stops hanging over you. You open by saying that you had a Meadowlark residential solar share on your house, that you cancelled it and it ended October 1st, and that you would like to pay off what you still owe on it today with your card. You speak plainly and a little apologetically, and you do not know any account or reference numbers by heart. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 6515550106, and if a second detail is needed your billing ZIP code, 12159; if they ask for your email instead it is marit.halvorsen@fastmail.com. You will not read a card or bank number out loud and you have nothing set up on file with Meadowlark; you expect to type your card into Meadowlark's secure payment page yourself. Only if the agent asks whether you hold anything else with Meadowlark do you mention that you are on their income-eligible waiting list for a new share; you hold nothing else. Only if the agent asks about the June charge or about any dispute do you say that on November 10th you filed a dispute about the June charge because the credit behind it looked off to you, and that you have not heard back yet. If the agent explains that something has to be added to or worked out on the account before they can give you the figure, you say that is fine and they should go ahead. When the agent tells you the amount to pay today and hands you the secure payment step, you complete it yourself with exactly that amount, choosing card as the method; you do not haggle over the figure or ask for anything to be taken off. Once the payment has gone through you thank the agent and say that is everything for today.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's customer profile from the phone number she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the customer reference number; nothing can be handled before the caller is found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record the in-session identity check with the two details the caller states (phone and billing ZIP).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before account details are discussed or any payment is taken.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the residential subscription: Meadowlark Standard 10, status closed on 2026-10-01, utility account, dual billing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The status closed decides the covered lines of the final-balance payment and the closed tier of its estimate share; the plan fixes late_fee_pct, estimate_wait_days and max_consecutive_estimates.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the National Grid utility account the subscription and the waitlist reservation both name.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Ties the waitlist reservation to this subscription's own utility account (the household-income tiers require the same account).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the projects: the subscription's NY_VDER project and the project the reservation queues for.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms both sit in the same utility territory under NY_VDER, a program the Income-Eligible Priority class serves.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the completed true-ups of contract years 1 and 2 (no_change, no guarantee credit).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Excludes any pending true-up credit or resize that would change the lines the final-balance payment covers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole billing ledger: actual charges (incl. the May re-post), the July estimate and its true-up, the open August estimate, the reversal correction, the February and June late fees, payments.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence of the estimate window, its reversal correction, the run of estimates, the overdue July charge and its late payment after the due date, the late fees counted by the repeat multiplier, and every line the payment covers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the credit lines: postings with kWh, value, banked value and dates, the May reversal and re-post, and the August posting of 2026-12-02 not yet priced.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The unpriced-line weight and credit-rate weight of the estimate, the pending-statement addition of the payment and the banked-share multiplier of the late fee rest on these lines; no September credit has posted.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the filing lines: initial 9.00 kW, subscriber decrease of 2.00 kW effective 2026-07-01, removal at closing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The capacity ratio of the estimate rests on the subscriber decrease that took effect within the estimate window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the subscriber requests, including the open billing dispute received 2026-11-10 naming the June 2026 charge.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The open dispute decides the standing of the estimate basis, the dispute hold of the payment and which open line the payment is recorded against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Income-Eligible Priority Waitlist reservation, queued on the same utility account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Cross-difficulty evidence of the household-income multiplier of the late fee and of the fee share of the payment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the customer holds no Meadowlark Access subscription.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Excludes the Access tier of the household-income ladders, leaving the waitlist tier.
